proposals.before: In the third month of Guangxu 5, after the rites at Emperor Tongzhi's Huiling mausoleum were completed, Principal Clerk Wu Kedup committed suicide in memorial protest to settle the question of imperial succession.
proposals.after: In the third month of Guangxu 5, after the rites at Emperor Tongzhi's Huiling mausoleum were completed, Principal Clerk Wu Kedu committed suicide in memorial protest to settle the question of imperial succession.
proposals.reason: Wu Kedup mistransliterates 吳可讀; 讀 is dú, so the established romanization is Wu Kedu.

proposals.before: Wu Kedup's memorial expressed precisely what the earlier edict had meant."
proposals.after: Wu Kedu's memorial expressed precisely what the earlier edict had meant."
proposals.reason: Same mistransliteration of 吳可讀 as Wu Kedup instead of Wu Kedu.

proposals.before: In the seventh year he was promoted to Grand Secretary and appointed educational commissioner of Jiangsu.
proposals.after: In the seventh year he was promoted to Academician of the Grand Secretariat and appointed educational commissioner of Jiangsu.
proposals.reason: 內閣學士 is not 大學士 (Grand Secretary); the idiomatic rendering collapses a distinct Grand Secretariat post.

proposals.before: Now, when Emperor Tongzhi was interred at Huiling, Principal Clerk Wu Kedup insisted that an heir be named for him and killed himself in protest; the court ordered a ministerial debate.
proposals.after: Now, when Emperor Tongzhi was interred at Huiling, Principal Clerk Wu Kedu insisted that an heir be named for him and remonstrated by suicide; the court ordered a ministerial debate.
proposals.reason: 吳可讀 romanizes as Wu Kedu, not Kedup; 以屍諫 is corpse/suicide remonstrance, which the idiomatic paraphrase blurs.

proposals.before: I deeply honor Wu Kedup's loyal sacrifice, yet regret that his final memorial did not fully express his intent.
proposals.after: I deeply grieve Wu Kedup's loyal death, yet regret that his final memorial did not fully express his intent.
proposals.reason: 竊痛 means to grieve over the death; idiomatic honor misrenders the verb against the Chinese and the literal.

proposals.before: In the seventh year he was appointed Grand Secretary and sent to preside over Fujian's provincial examination.
proposals.after: In the seventh year he was appointed Academician of the Grand Secretariat and sent to preside over Fujian's provincial examination.
proposals.reason: 內閣學士 is Academician of the Grand Secretariat, not Grand Secretary.

proposals.before: In the seventh year he was appointed Grand Secretary and went out to preside over the Fujian provincial examination.
proposals.after: In the seventh year he was appointed Academician of the Grand Secretariat and went out to preside over the Fujian provincial examination.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 內閣學士 as Grand Secretary in the literal English.

proposals.before: Minister Peng Yulin repeatedly declined office and would not accept appointment; he impeached him for scheming personal convenience and opening the way for meritorious ministers' arrogance.
proposals.after: Minister Peng Yulin repeatedly declined office and would not accept appointment; Sheng Yu impeached him for scheming personal convenience and opening the way for meritorious ministers' arrogance.
proposals.reason: Literal English leaves the silent subject of 劾 as an ambiguous he, which can be misread as Peng Yulin; the Chinese continuation makes Sheng Yu the impeaching subject.

proposals.before: Such as Vice Ministers He Shouci and Ministers Wan Qingli and Dong Xun—all were impeached and removed.
proposals.after: Such as Vice Minister He Shouci and Ministers Wan Qingli and Dong Xun—all were impeached and removed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 侍郎賀壽慈 is a single vice minister; plural Vice Ministers wrongly multiplies He Shouci's office.

proposals.before: Peilun fled to the foot of Mount Gu, and the villagers refused him, saying: "I am the commissioner in charge!"
proposals.after: Peilun fled to the foot of Mount Gu, and the villagers refused him; he said: "I am the commissioner in charge!"
proposals.reason: The quote 我會辦大臣也 is Peilun identifying himself after being refused; the literal English wrongly makes the villagers the speakers of that first-person claim.

proposals.before: He Ruzhang, whose courtesy name was Zijin, was a native of Dapu in Guangdong.
proposals.after: He Ruzhang, whose courtesy name was Ziguan, was a native of Dapu in Guangdong.
proposals.reason: Courtesy name 子瓘 is Ziguan, not Zijin; the English spelling does not match the Chinese characters.

proposals.before: He Ruzhang, courtesy name Zijin, was registered in Dapu, Guangdong.
proposals.after: He Ruzhang, courtesy name Ziguan, was registered in Dapu, Guangdong.
proposals.reason: Courtesy name 子瓘 is Ziguan, not Zijin; the English spelling does not match the Chinese characters.

proposals.before: Soon he and Vice Director Pan Yantong secretly submitted five stratagems for probing the enemy, and also impeached Li Hongzhang's memorial fixing peace, resenting Liu Yongfu's willingness to fight—he spoke with utmost indignation.
proposals.after: Soon he and Vice Director Pan Yantong secretly submitted five stratagems for probing the enemy, and also impeached Li Hongzhang's memorial fixing peace; resenting [Li's] jealousy of Liu Yongfu's daring to fight, he spoke with utmost indignation.
proposals.reason: Chinese 嫉劉永福敢戰 marks resentment at hostility toward Liu Yongfu's fighting spirit, not resentment of Liu himself.

proposals.before: If we divide our forces into three columns and strike Vietnam swiftly, they will be too busy defending themselves to aid Taiwan—the superior stratagem.
proposals.after: If we divide our forces into three columns and strike Vietnam swiftly, they will be too busy saving themselves—the superior stratagem.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents 'to aid Taiwan'; Chinese only says the enemy will be too busy saving themselves.

proposals.before: He was appointed Chief of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and served as Minister of the Zongli Yamen for Foreign Affairs.
proposals.after: He was appointed Chief of the Court of State Ceremonial (Honglu Temple) and served as Minister of the Zongli Yamen for Foreign Affairs.
proposals.reason: 鴻臚寺卿 is the Court of State Ceremonial, not the Court of Imperial Sacrifices (太常寺).

proposals.before: He was appointed Chief of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and served as Minister of the Zongli Yamen for Foreign Affairs.
proposals.after: He was appointed Chief of the Court of State Ceremonial (Honglu Temple) and served as Minister of the Zongli Yamen for Foreign Affairs.
proposals.reason: 鴻臚寺卿 is mistranslated as Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

proposals.before: Bourée wanted to survey the old boundary first; Chengxiu, citing the treaty, insisted on correcting the line first, and neither would yield. Bourée openly offered Wenzhou, Baole, and Haining to China while secretly cabling his minister in Beijing to accuse Chengxiu of violating the treaty, warning that unless the old boundary were surveyed first talks would collapse.
proposals.after: Bourée wanted to survey the old boundary first; Chengxiu, citing the treaty, insisted on correcting the line first, and neither would yield. Bourée openly offered Wenyuan, Baole, and Haining to China while secretly cabling his minister in Beijing to accuse Chengxiu of violating the treaty, warning that unless the old boundary were surveyed first talks would collapse.
proposals.reason: 文淵 is the border place Wenyuan, not Wenzhou (溫州).

proposals.before: Bourée wished to survey the old boundary first; Chengxiu, citing the treaty, insisted on correcting the boundary first, and neither would yield. Bourée openly offered to return Wenzhou, Baole, and Haining to us, while secretly cabling his minister in Beijing to denounce Chengxiu for violating the treaty and contending obstinately, saying that unless the old boundary were surveyed first negotiations would be broken off.
proposals.after: Bourée wished to survey the old boundary first; Chengxiu, citing the treaty, insisted on correcting the boundary first, and neither would yield. Bourée openly offered to return Wenyuan, Baole, and Haining to us, while secretly cabling his minister in Beijing to denounce Chengxiu for violating the treaty and contending obstinately, saying that unless the old boundary were surveyed first negotiations would be broken off.
proposals.reason: 文淵 mistranslated as Wenzhou.

proposals.before: Neither Qulü nor Wenzhou can be held; the pass loses its strategic value and both attack and defense become impossible—the first harm.
proposals.after: Neither Qulü nor Wenyuan can be held; the pass loses its strategic value and both attack and defense become impossible—the first harm.
proposals.reason: 文淵 is Wenyuan, not Wenzhou.

proposals.before: Neither Qulü nor Wenzhou can be secured; the pass loses its strategic advantage and both offense and defense become difficult—the first harm.
proposals.after: Neither Qulü nor Wenyuan can be secured; the pass loses its strategic advantage and both offense and defense become difficult—the first harm.
proposals.reason: 文淵 mistranslated as Wenzhou.

proposals.before: Lose Wenzhou and there is no buffer to the north; inland trade will be squeezed, Vietnam will be gone—how then can Guangdong be saved?
proposals.after: Lose Wenyuan and there is no buffer to the north; inland trade will be squeezed, Vietnam will be gone—how then can Guangdong be saved?
proposals.reason: 文淵 is Wenyuan, not Wenzhou.

proposals.before: Once Wenzhou is lost there is not an inch of land to the north; inland trade will be coerced, Vietnam will no longer exist—how can Guangdong be preserved?
proposals.after: Once Wenyuan is lost there is not an inch of land to the north; inland trade will be coerced, Vietnam will no longer exist—how can Guangdong be preserved?
proposals.reason: 文淵 mistranslated as Wenzhou.

proposals.before: In the twelfth year the French sent Dillon and Descours to negotiate in Bourée's place.
proposals.after: In the twelfth year the French separately sent Dillon and Descours to meet.
proposals.reason: Chinese 別遣…來會 does not state they replaced Bourée; 'in Bourée's place' is invented.

proposals.before: He rose to Grand Secretary and was appointed educational commissioner of the capital district.
proposals.after: He rose to Academician of the Grand Secretariat and was appointed educational commissioner of Shuntian.
proposals.reason: 內閣學士 is Academician of the Grand Secretariat, not Grand Secretary (大學士).

proposals.before: He was promoted in succession to Grand Secretary and appointed educational commissioner of Shuntian.
proposals.after: He was promoted in succession to Academician of the Grand Secretariat and appointed educational commissioner of Shuntian.
proposals.reason: 內閣學士 mistranslated as Grand Secretary.

proposals.before: When the Shandong missionary case broke out, the German envoy Heinig demanded that Li Bingheng be removed from office.
proposals.after: When the Shandong missionary case broke out, the German envoy Heyking demanded that Li Bingheng be removed from office.
proposals.reason: 海靖 is the German envoy Baron von Heyking; 'Heinig' is a clear mistransliteration of the established name.

proposals.before: When the Shandong missionary case arose, the German envoy Heinig pressed for dismissal of Li Bingheng from office.
proposals.after: When the Shandong missionary case arose, the German envoy Heyking pressed for dismissal of Li Bingheng from office.
proposals.reason: Same mistransliteration of 海靖 as Heinig instead of Heyking in the literal field.

proposals.before: Only Sheng Yu spoke with restraint and withdrew early to preserve his integrity—perhaps he alone, standing apart, did not betray the reputation of the Qingliu?
proposals.after: Only Sheng Yu spoke with restraint and withdrew early to preserve his integrity—perhaps he alone, standing apart, did not betray his pure reputation?
proposals.reason: 清譽 means 'pure reputation', not the Qingliu faction; the idiomatic rendering invents a Qingliu reference absent from the Chinese.

decisions.reason: 吳可讀 romanizes as Wu Kedu (讀 = dú); 'Wu Kedup' is a clear transliteration error, and the proposed replacement is accurate.
Same unit chain repeats 吳可讀 as Wu Kedup; correcting to Wu Kedu restores the established romanization.
內閣學士 is Academician of the Grand Secretariat, not 大學士 (Grand Secretary); the proposed office title corrects a real conflation.
吳可讀 is Wu Kedu, and 以屍諫 is remonstrance by suicide/corpse; the proposal fixes both the name and the blurred remonstrance sense.

decisions.reason: 竊痛 means to grieve, so 'honor' is wrong; the proposal still leaves Wu Kedup, so revise to grieve and restore Wu Kedu.
授內閣學士 again names the Grand Secretariat academician post, not Grand Secretary; the proposed title is correct.
Literal repeats the same 內閣學士/Grand Secretary error; Academician of the Grand Secretariat is required.
Silent-subject 劾 continues Sheng Yu's impeachments from the prior units; ambiguous 'he' risks reading Peng as the impeacher, and naming Sheng Yu is required.

decisions.reason: 侍郎賀壽慈 marks one vice minister; plural 'Vice Ministers' invents multiple officeholders for He Shouci.
After 鄉人拒之, 曰：「我會辦大臣也！」 is Peilun's first-person self-identification; attributing the quote to the villagers is a dialogue error.

decisions.reason: 字子瓘 uses 瓘 (guàn); Zijin does not match the characters, and Ziguan is the correct courtesy-name romanization.
Literal likewise misspells 子瓘 as Zijin; Ziguan restores the matching romanization.

decisions.after: Soon he and Vice Director Pan Yantong secretly submitted five stratagems for probing the enemy, and also impeached Li Hongzhang's memorial fixing peace; resenting Li's jealousy of Liu Yongfu's daring to fight, he spoke with utmost indignation.
decisions.reason: 嫉劉永福敢戰 condemns hostility toward Liu's daring to fight, not resentment of Liu; the proposal is right on sense but the bracketed '[Li's]' is awkward, so revise to name Li cleanly.

decisions.reason: 彼將自救不暇 says only that the enemy will be too busy saving themselves; 'to aid Taiwan' is invented and must be removed.
鴻臚寺卿 is the Court of State Ceremonial (Honglu Temple), not 太常寺 (Court of Imperial Sacrifices); the proposed office is correct.
Literal repeats the same 鴻臚寺/太常寺 office error; Court of State Ceremonial is required.
文淵 is the Sino-Vietnamese border place Wenyuan, not 溫州 (Wenzhou); the proposed place-name corrects a real misidentification.
Literal likewise renders 文淵 as Wenzhou; Wenyuan is the required place name.
Again 文淵, not Wenzhou; the strategic-harm sentence must name Wenyuan.
Literal repeats the Wenzhou misreading of 文淵; Wenyuan is correct.
文淵既失 continues the same place; replacing Wenzhou with Wenyuan restores the source geography.
Literal again misreads 文淵 as Wenzhou; Wenyuan matches the Chinese.

decisions.reason: 累遷內閣學士 is Academician of the Grand Secretariat, not Grand Secretary, and 督順天學政 is Shuntian; both proposed corrections match the Chinese.

decisions.reason: Literal likewise mistranslates 內閣學士 as Grand Secretary; Academician of the Grand Secretariat is required.
